findings.title: Defer focus refresh while a session mutation owns the state
findings.problem: Only quiet loads respect running.current. Focus invokes load() with quiet=false, increments the same generation as POST/DELETE, and supersedes the mutation completion. A GET started before the mutation commits can therefore become the authoritative response even after the mutation succeeds.
reproduction: Display an authenticated admin profile; hold DELETE /api/session before it resolves.
Dispatch window focus. Let its GET capture the old profile/permissions but delay that GET response.
Resolve DELETE successfully. session() skips accept(null) because the GET incremented generation.
Resolve the stale GET: old profile and administration links are displayed despite completed sign-out, until a subsequent refresh.
Analogous guest-entry case: focus GET captures 401 while POST is pending; successful POST is discarded and the UI remains signed out.
findings.impact: Client session/navigation becomes inconsistent with the committed cookie/server session. Existing backend authorization still protects private mutations; this is not a demonstrated server privilege bypass.
findings.requiredChange: Skip or queue external focus/refresh requests during POST/DELETE, retain mutation ownership, and perform at most one authoritative post-mutation refresh. Preserve invalidation of reads that began before the mutation. Add delayed GET/DELETE and GET/POST tests in both relevant completion orders.
